15-A person finds a web page worth keeping and saves its address. The app automatically collects the page's title, description, favicon, and preview image so the saved entry is rich and recognisable without manual effort. The bookmark then appears in their list.
16-
17:**Why this priority**: Saving links with useful, automatically captured detail is the core reason the app exists. This single story is a usable MVP: capture a link and see a recognisable entry in a list.
18-
19-**Independent Test**: Add a bookmark by entering a URL, then confirm it appears in the list showing the automatically collected title, description, and favicon, and remains after reloading the app.
20-
21-**Acceptance Scenarios**:
22-
23:1. **Given** an empty bookmark list, **When** the user submits a valid URL, **Then** the app fetches the page's title, description, favicon, and preview image and presents the collected title and description for the user to adjust before the initial save.
24-2. **Given** the user has reviewed the automatically collected title and description, **When** they change either and save, **Then** the bookmark is stored with the user's adjusted values.
25-3. **Given** the target page provides no title or description, **When** the bookmark is saved, **Then** the app falls back to a readable derived title (e.g. from the address) so the entry is never blank.
26-4. **Given** the user submits an entry that is not a valid web address, **When** they try to save, **Then** the app rejects it with a clear message and saves nothing.
--
55-
56-1. **Given** an existing bookmark, **When** the user edits its address, title, description, tags, or note and saves, **Then** the updated values are shown and persist across reloads.
57-2. **Given** the user edits the address to one that already exists on another bookmark, **When** they save, **Then** the app warns of the conflict and does not create a duplicate.
58:3. **Given** a note written in Markdown, **When** the user saves and later views the bookmark, **Then** the Markdown is stored verbatim and rendered as formatted text when displayed.

86-**Acceptance Scenarios**:
87-
88-1. **Given** saved bookmarks, **When** the user searches plain text, **Then** results include bookmarks whose title, description, note, or address contain that text, matched case-insensitively.
89:2. **Given** the user enters `#tagname`, **When** the search runs, **Then** results are limited to bookmarks carrying that tag.
90:3. **Given** the user enters ordinary text and a `#tag` together (e.g. `report #news`), **When** the search runs, **Then** both conditions must hold — only bookmarks that match the text AND carry the tag are returned.
91-4. **Given** the user enters a phrase in double quotes, **When** the search runs, **Then** only bookmarks containing that exact phrase match.
92:5. **Given** the user quotes a word that is also an operator (e.g. `"AND"`), **When** the search runs, **Then** the quoted word is treated as a literal search term, not as a boolean operator.
93-6. **Given** the user combines terms with `AND`, `OR`, `NOT`, and parentheses, **When** the search runs, **Then** results honour the boolean logic and grouping.
94-7. **Given** a search that matches nothing, **When** results are shown, **Then** a clear "no matching bookmarks" state is displayed.

134-**Why this priority**: Bulk maintenance keeps a large collection manageable and is explicitly required by the client.
135-
136:**Independent Test**: Select multiple bookmarks (and separately "select all matching current search"), add a tag to the selection, confirm all gained it; then archive the selection and confirm they leave the normal list.
137-
138-**Acceptance Scenarios**:
139-
140-1. **Given** several bookmarks, **When** the user selects them individually and adds or removes a tag, **Then** every selected bookmark reflects the change.
141:2. **Given** an active view, **When** the user chooses "select all matching", **Then** the selection covers every bookmark in the complete current view — honouring its search text, tag include/exclude filters, and whether the user is in the unread or archive view — not only the bookmarks on the visible page.
142-3. **Given** a multi-selection, **When** the user marks read/unread, archives, or deletes, **Then** the action applies to all selected bookmarks, with deletion requiring confirmation.

181-A person keeps a preserved copy of a bookmarked page so its content survives even if the original changes or disappears. When the link is a PDF, the original file is saved. The user can also request preservation through the Internet Archive.
182-
183:**Why this priority**: Protects against link rot; important to the client but the collection is usable before it exists.
184-
185-**Independent Test**: Save a bookmark, request a preserved copy, and confirm the preserved content can be opened later; save a PDF link and confirm the original file is retained; trigger Internet Archive preservation and confirm a reference to the archived snapshot is stored.
186-
187-**Acceptance Scenarios**:
188-
189:1. **Given** a bookmarked web page, **When** the user requests preservation, **Then** the app stores the page as a single self-contained local HTML file (with its needed assets inlined) associated with the bookmark, openable offline.
190-2. **Given** a bookmarked address that points to a PDF, **When** it is preserved, **Then** the original PDF file is saved instead of an HTML copy and can be reopened.
191-3. **Given** a bookmark, **When** the user requests Internet Archive preservation, **Then** the app submits it and stores a link to the resulting archived snapshot.
192-4. **Given** preservation cannot be completed (source unreachable or service unavailable), **When** the attempt fails, **Then** the bookmark is unaffected and the user is told preservation did not succeed.

244-- **FR-001**: Users MUST be able to save a bookmark by providing a web address.
245-- **FR-002**: System MUST validate that a submitted address is a well-formed web URL and reject invalid entries with a clear message.
246-- **FR-003**: On save, System MUST automatically fetch the page's title, description, favicon, and preview image when available.
247:- **FR-003a**: System MUST let the user review and adjust the automatically collected title and description before the initial save, as well as edit them later.
248-- **FR-004**: System MUST derive a readable title and save the bookmark even when page metadata cannot be fetched, indicating that metadata is unavailable.
249-- **FR-005**: When a submitted address matches an existing bookmark, System MUST open the existing bookmark for editing rather than creating a duplicate.
250-
--
252-
253-- **FR-006**: Users MUST be able to edit a bookmark's address, title, description, tags, and note.
254-- **FR-007**: System MUST prevent edits that would create two bookmarks with the same address, warning the user of the conflict.
255:- **FR-008**: System MUST accept notes written in Markdown, store the Markdown source verbatim, and render it as formatted text when the bookmark is displayed.
256-
257-**Listing, sorting & opening**
258-
--
264-**Search**
265-
266-- **FR-013**: System MUST provide case-insensitive search across each bookmark's title, description, note, and address.
267:- **FR-014**: Search MUST support `#tag` terms that restrict results to bookmarks carrying that tag; when ordinary text and one or more `#tag` terms appear together, all MUST match (they are combined with AND).
268:- **FR-015**: Search MUST support exact phrase matching via double-quoted text, and MUST treat a quoted word that is also an operator (e.g. `"AND"`, `"OR"`, `"NOT"`) as a literal search term rather than a boolean operator.
269-- **FR-016**: Search MUST support boolean combination of terms using AND, OR, NOT, and parentheses for grouping (operator words outside quotes).
270-- **FR-017**: System MUST report invalid queries (e.g. unbalanced quotes or parentheses) rather than returning misleading results.
271-
--
282-
283-**Bulk actions**
284-
285:- **FR-023**: Users MUST be able to select multiple bookmarks individually, and to "select all matching" the complete current view — respecting active search text, tag include/exclude filters, and whether the unread or archive view is active — not merely the bookmarks on the visible page.
286-- **FR-024**: Users MUST be able to apply to a selection: add or remove tags, mark read or unread, archive, and delete.
287-- **FR-025**: Destructive bulk actions (delete) MUST require confirmation.
288-
--
300-
301-**Page preservation**
302-
303:- **FR-032**: Users MUST be able to request a preserved copy of a bookmarked page, stored as a single self-contained local HTML file (needed assets inlined) that can be opened offline.
304:- **FR-033**: When a bookmarked address points to a PDF, System MUST preserve the original PDF file instead of an HTML copy, and allow it to be reopened.
305-- **FR-034**: Users MUST be able to request preservation through the Internet Archive and have a link to the resulting snapshot stored with the bookmark.
306-- **FR-035**: When a preservation attempt fails, System MUST leave the bookmark unaffected and inform the user it did not complete.
307-
--
318-
319-### Key Entities *(include if feature involves data)*
320-
321:- **Bookmark**: A saved link. Attributes: web address, title, description, note (Markdown source), favicon, preview image, set of tags, date added, read/unread state, archived state, references to any preserved copy / saved PDF / Internet Archive snapshot.
322-- **Tag**: A short label grouping related bookmarks. A bookmark may carry several tags; a tag may apply to many bookmarks. The set of tags in use drives tag suggestions and tag filters.
323-- **Saved Search**: A named, revisitable combination of search text plus included and excluded tags.
324:- **Preserved Copy**: Stored content associated with a bookmark — a single self-contained local HTML file capturing the page, or (for PDF addresses) the original PDF file, and/or a link to an Internet Archive snapshot.
325-- **Preferences**: The user's persisted display settings (default sort, items per page, text size).
326-
327-## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*
--
333-- **SC-003**: 100% of saved bookmarks, tags, notes, read/archive states, and saved searches remain present and correct after the app is closed and reopened.
334-- **SC-004**: Search and filter results update within 1 second of the user finishing their input for a collection of at least 1,000 bookmarks.
335-- **SC-005**: A boolean/phrase/tag search returns results consistent with the stated logic in 100% of defined acceptance cases.
336:- **SC-006**: A user can apply a bulk action to all items matching a search of at least 200 matches in a single operation.
337-- **SC-007**: Importing a standard browser-bookmark HTML file preserves 100% of titles, tags, and dates for valid entries, and exported files re-import without loss.
338-- **SC-008**: 95% of first-time users successfully save, find, and re-open a bookmark without external help.
339-
--
342-- Single-user, personal use; no login/accounts, sharing, collaboration, or browser extension (confirmed by client).
343-- The app runs as a web application accessed through a browser.
344-- Bookmarks and preserved copies are retained indefinitely; no automatic expiry.
345:- Notes are authored and stored as Markdown (source kept verbatim) and rendered as formatted text on display; no separate rich-text editor is provided.
346-- Automatic metadata capture depends on the target page being reachable and providing standard title/description/preview information; missing data falls back to derived values.
347-- Internet Archive preservation depends on the external Internet Archive service being reachable; unavailability is reported, not fatal.
348-- Import/export targets the widely used Netscape-style browser-bookmark HTML format; tag preservation relies on tag data being present in the file.
